pset
label: Planets
description: Which planets the orrery shows, from the Sun out: the inner planets to the Earth, to Mars, to Jupiter or to Saturn (the planets known before 1781)

name: moon
label: Moon
description: The Moon round the Earth, driven by its own train (sidereal month) and an idler under the Earth's arm, so it keeps its direction in space as the Earth goes round

name: acc
label: Accuracy target
description: The largest error of any body's period. The smallest gearbox whose trains all meet it is chosen (a tighter target needs more teeth)

name: maxTeeth
label: Most teeth per gear
description: The largest gear the trains may use (60 to 120). Its least value is the least that meets the accuracy target for these planets

name: moduleSize
label: Module
description: Tooth size of every gear: pitch diameter = module x teeth. The whole gearbox scales with it

name: material
label: Gears made by
description: 3D printed gears 4 mm thick, or laser-cut from 3 mm acrylic or 4 mm plywood (the named face set Cut sheet lays every gear and the base plate out for the laser)

name: rIn
label: Mercury's arm
description: Radius of Mercury's orbit. The others follow outwards; not to scale (see the README)

name: gapO
label: Gap between orbits
description: Least room between the balls, arms and pins of neighbouring orbits

name: size
label: Ball size
description: Scale of the Sun and the planets (the Sun 24 mm across at 1); ordered by size, not to scale

name: days
label: Days since 1 Jan 2000
description: Turn the crank: one turn is one sidereal year (365.256 days). Day 0 is 1 January 2000, 12:00 TT (J2000), with every body at its mean longitude then; -36525 is 1900, 36525 is 2100

title: Geared orrery
description: A hand-cranked orrery: the Sun, Mercury to Saturn on nested tubes, the Moon round the Earth as an option, each driven from one crank through two gear stages whose tooth counts were searched so its period matches the real sidereal period within the accuracy target (one crank turn is one year). Choose the planets, the target, the most teeth per gear, the module, printed or laser-cut gears and the arms; turn the date and every ball moves to its place by its gears. Involute teeth (20 deg), assertions on the trains, the meshing, the clearances and the planets' places. The cut sheet holds every gear for a laser.
author: 3DCraft Jigs
